meta.author: Hubert Labs
meta.how_to_use: Save this file at the repo root as PROJECT_SPEC.json. In Claude Code, run: 'Read PROJECT_SPEC.json in full. Follow execution_protocol exactly. Start with phase 0 and stop at the end of each phase for my review.'

role: You are a principal full-stack engineer and solutions architect building a production-grade travel booking platform (web + mobile + admin) on one shared backend. You write strict TypeScript, clean architecture, tested code, and you treat security, payments and money handling as first-class concerns.
objective: Build 'Suskii Travels and Tour', a fast, trustworthy, deal-focused one-stop travel shop (flights, hotels, packages, tours, visa, travel add-ons) delivered as a Next.js website, an Expo React Native app for iOS and Android, and a Next.js admin console, all consuming a single NestJS API backed by PostgreSQL and Redis.

rules: Before writing code, create CLAUDE.md at the repo root summarising this spec, the architecture, conventions and commands. Keep it updated at the end of every phase.
Execute phases strictly in order (see 'phases'). Never start phase N+1 until phase N meets all its acceptance_criteria.
At the start of each phase, write a short plan (files to create or change, risks) to docs/phases/phase-<n>.md, then implement.

At the end of each phase: run lint, typecheck, unit tests and build for every affected workspace; fix all failures; update CHANGELOG.md; make one conventional commit per logical unit (feat:, fix:, chore:, etc.); then STOP and print a phase report: what was built, how to run it, test results, open issues, and decisions that need my input.
Never invent supplier credentials, API keys or business facts. Use .env.example placeholders and mock adapters until real credentials are provided.
Never hardcode secrets. Never commit .env files. Never log PII, tokens, passport numbers or payment data.
If a requirement is ambiguous, pick the most secure and conventional option, record it in docs/decisions/ADR-<nnn>-<title>.md, and continue.
Prefer small, reviewable diffs. No placeholder 'TODO: implement' code in completed phases; stubs are allowed only behind clearly named mock adapters.
Use the design tokens in 'design_system' as the single source of truth. Do not hardcode colors, radii or font sizes in components.
developer_environment_notes: Primary dev machine is Windows (PowerShell). All scripts must be cross-platform (use Node scripts or pnpm scripts, not bash-only). Provide docker-compose for local Postgres and Redis.
iOS builds must go through Expo EAS Build cloud runners (no local Xcode).

product.name: Suskii Travels and Tour
product.positioning: Your one-stop travel shop: flights, hotels, packages, tours, visas and add-ons with honest prices and flexible payment.
product.hero_subheadline: Cheap flights, great hotels, holiday packages and visa support, all in one place, with flexible payment on every booking.
product.primary_market: Nigeria, then wider Africa, then global

locales.note: i18n-ready from day one (all strings in message catalogs); add fr and pcm later.

brand_and_compliance_guardrails.summary: The visual language is inspired by the provided design system reference. The product is Suskii, not Wakanow.
rules: Never use the Wakanow name, logo, imagery, copy, 'Wakanow Prime' naming or any of their trademarks. The membership program is 'Suskii Prime'.
Trust signals must be config-driven, never hardcoded: store them in the CMS/settings table with fields {label, value, verified: boolean, evidence_url}. Only render items where verified=true.

Seed trust signals as: '24/7 support' (verified=true), 'Flexible payment on every booking' (verified=true), 'Secure payments' (verified=true), 'Travellers served' (value='2M+', verified=false), 'IATA accredited' (verified=false). IATA accreditation and traveller counts are regulated or factual claims; they stay hidden until the business provides proof.
All prices shown on deal cards must come from a real or clearly-labelled mock quote with a 'from' qualifier and a 'last updated' timestamp; never show fabricated fares in production.
Comply with the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA) and GDPR for EU users: consent capture, privacy policy, data subject request endpoints (export, delete), data retention policy.
PCI DSS: the platform must never see or store raw card data. Use provider-hosted checkout or tokenised fields (target SAQ-A scope).

monorepo.why: One repo, shared TypeScript types, Zod schemas, API client, design tokens and i18n across web, mobile and admin; cached builds in CI.

web.framework: Next.js 15+ (App Router, React Server Components, TypeScript strict)
web.styling: Tailwind CSS with a shared preset generated from design tokens
web.ui_primitives: Radix UI primitives wrapped in own components (accessible, unstyled)
web.data: TanStack Query for client state from the API; RSC fetches for SEO pages
web.why: SSR/ISR for SEO-heavy deal and destination pages, edge caching, strong Core Web Vitals.

mobile.framework: Expo (latest SDK) + Expo Router + React Native, TypeScript strict
mobile.styling: NativeWind using the same Tailwind preset from packages/design-tokens
mobile.storage: expo-secure-store for tokens; MMKV for non-sensitive cache
mobile.builds: EAS Build + EAS Submit + EAS Update (OTA for JS-only fixes)
mobile.why: Maximum code sharing with web (types, schemas, API client, tokens), OTA updates, cloud iOS builds.

admin.framework: Next.js (separate app: apps/admin) with RBAC-gated routes
admin.why: Operations, bookings, refunds, content and deals management without touching the database directly.

backend.framework: NestJS (TypeScript, modular monolith with clear bounded-context modules)
backend.api_style: REST, versioned under /v1, OpenAPI 3.1 spec generated and used to generate the typed client in packages/api-client
backend.validation: Zod schemas from packages/shared (nestjs-zod) so web, mobile and API validate identically
backend.search_autocomplete: PostgreSQL pg_trgm + unaccent over an airports/cities table (IATA codes); upgrade to Typesense only if latency requires
backend.why: Modular monolith is the fastest path to production with clean seams to split services later (search, booking, payments) if scale demands.

data.object_storage: S3-compatible (AWS S3 or GCS) for images, e-tickets, visa documents; signed URLs only
data.cdn_images: Next/Image + CDN; mobile uses expo-image with caching

integrations.flights: Adapter pattern: FlightSupplier interface. Implement MockFlightSupplier first, then DuffelFlightSupplier. Leave AmadeusFlightSupplier and a GDS/consolidator adapter as pluggable options.
integrations.hotels: HotelSupplier interface. MockHotelSupplier first, then one real provider (e.g. Duffel Stays or Hotelbeds) chosen via ADR.
integrations.tours_packages_visa_addons: Managed in-house via admin (inventory owned by Suskii); add-ons include travel insurance, airport transfer, eSIM, lounge access, extra baggage, seat selection.
integrations.payments: PaymentProvider interface. Paystack and Flutterwave for NGN/African cards, bank transfer and USSD; Stripe for international cards. Webhook-driven confirmation.
integrations.fx: Exchange-rate provider behind an FxProvider interface, cached in Redis with timestamp; always charge in a single settled currency per booking.
integrations.email: Resend or AWS SES via EmailProvider interface; React Email templates
integrations.sms_whatsapp: Termii (Nigeria) and/or Twilio via MessagingProvider interface
integrations.maps: Optional; only for hotel detail pages
integrations.support: Live chat widget slot + WhatsApp click-to-chat; ticketing handled in admin

infra.containers: Docker multi-stage builds for api, web, admin; distroless or alpine runtime, non-root user
infra.default_hosting: API on GCP Cloud Run or AWS ECS Fargate; web and admin on Vercel or as containers; managed Postgres (Cloud SQL / RDS) and managed Redis (Memorystore / ElastiCache)
infra.kubernetes_option: Provide a Helm chart under infra/helm for teams that prefer GKE/EKS; not required for launch
infra.iac: Terraform modules under infra/terraform, cloud-agnostic variables where possible
infra.edge: Cloudflare in front of web and API: WAF, bot management, DDoS protection, Turnstile

repo_layout.packages/design-tokens: Tokens as TS + generated Tailwind preset + CSS variables
repo_layout.packages/ui-web: Web component library built on tokens
repo_layout.packages/ui-native: React Native component library built on tokens

backend_modules: cms (banners, trust signals, destination content, FAQs)
key_principles: Supplier adapters isolate third-party APIs; domain code never imports vendor SDKs directly.
Money is stored as integer minor units (BIGINT) with an ISO-4217 currency code; never use floats.
All timestamps stored in UTC; flight departure/arrival also store the airport's IANA timezone and local time.
Every write endpoint that creates bookings, payments or refunds requires an Idempotency-Key header (stored in Redis/Postgres for 24h).
Bookings are driven by an explicit state machine; transitions are persisted and audited.
Search results are cached in Redis by a normalised query hash with short TTLs; offers carry an expiry and are re-priced before payment.

critical_rules: Re-price with the supplier immediately before payment; if price changed, show the difference and require explicit re-consent.

If payment succeeds but supplier ticketing/confirmation fails or times out, move to TICKETING and let the reconciliation worker retry with backoff; after the retry budget, auto-initiate a refund and notify the customer and ops.
Webhooks are the source of truth for payment status; client redirects only trigger a status poll.
Hold deadlines from suppliers drive automatic EXPIRED transitions and customer reminders.

Traveller (saved passengers: names as on passport, DOB, nationality, passport number encrypted, expiry)
SearchLog (anonymised), Offer (supplier offer snapshot with expiry)
Booking, BookingItem (flight | hotel | package | tour | visa | addon), BookingPassenger, BookingStatusHistory
Package, Tour, TourDeparture, VisaProduct, VisaApplication, VisaDocument, Addon
AuditLog, IdempotencyKey, WebhookEvent (deduplicated by provider event id)

design_system.source: https://gitreverse.com/designs/wakanow-com (visual inspiration only; apply to the Suskii brand)
design_system.feel: Clean, fast, commercial, trust-first, deal-focused. Utility-first booking UI. Medium-to-high density but scannable. No heavy gradients, glassmorphism or decorative effects.

color.notes: Derived hover/pressed/muted/status shades must pass WCAG 2.2 AA contrast; verify with an automated contrast test. White text on #F7941D is below 4.5:1 for small text, so orange buttons use bold text at >=16px or dark text (#0D1520) where needed.

typography.loading: next/font on web (self-hosted, no layout shift); expo-font on mobile
typography.note: Reference shows ~11px body; use 16px body for readability and accessibility, 14px for dense metadata.

components.button_secondary: Orange fill, used for promos and secondary CTAs only (e.g. 'Join Suskii Prime', 'View deal')
components.button_ghost: Transparent, blue text, for tertiary actions
components.input: White fill, 1px border token, radius md, no shadow, visible 2px focus ring, 48px height, icon slot left
components.tabs: Vertical-category tabs with icon + label; active tab has blue text and 3px blue underline; horizontally scrollable on mobile
components.segmented_control: Pill-style for trip type (Round trip / One way / Multi-city)
components.card: White surface, radius lg, 1px border or flat, hover lifts with card_hover shadow on desktop only
components.deal_card: Image top (16:9), route 'LOS → LHR', airline logo + name, dates, cabin, strong price 'from ₦X' in primary, optional orange discount badge, 'last updated' meta, CTA
components.destination_card: Image with dark bottom scrim, city + country, 'N hotels', 'from ₦X/night'
components.badge: Orange for promo/savings, blue-tint for info, green for 'Free cancellation'
components.trust_bar: Icon + short label row, 2x2 grid on mobile, single row on desktop
components.skeleton: Shimmer-free subtle pulse skeletons for every async card and result list

design_system.imagery: Licensed or royalty-free destination photography only (e.g. Unsplash/Pexels with attribution where required); served as AVIF/WebP with blur placeholders.

Light sky background (#F2F6F9) with a subtle destination image or illustration on desktop right side. Headline 'Your one-stop travel shop' (Plus Jakarta Sans, bold). Subheadline. Trust bar directly beneath: verified trust signals from CMS (see guardrails).
sections_in_order.mobile: Headline 34px, image hidden or reduced, search card immediately visible without scrolling past fold.

travellers: adults (1-9), children 2-11, infants under 2 (infants <= adults, total <= 9)
optional: direct flights only, flexible dates +/- 3 days

flights_form.behaviour: Persist last search locally; serialise search to URL query params for shareable/SEO-friendly results pages.

sections_in_order.packages_form: Destination, month or date range, travellers, budget range.

Heading 'Fresh flight offers' + 'See all deals' link. Filter chips by origin city (Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt, Accra, Nairobi). Horizontal scroll carousel on mobile, 4-column grid on desktop. Deal cards per design_system.deal_card, sourced from the deals service (worker refreshes cached lowest fares on popular routes). Each card links to a pre-filled search.

Simple orange-accented block: 'Save more with Suskii Prime', 3 benefits (member-only fares, fee waivers, priority support), price per month/year from CMS, orange 'Join Suskii Prime' CTA, 'Learn more' ghost link.
Three-step explainer of how flexible payment / book-on-hold works, with honest terms (see features.flexible_payment).
Curated holiday packages and tours cards with 'from' price per person.
4 value props with icons: best-price focus, flexible payment, 24/7 human support, secure payments.
App Store / Google Play badges (only link when live), QR code on desktop.
Email + optional WhatsApp opt-in for deal alerts; double opt-in; consent checkbox; Turnstile protection.
Collapsible FAQ and popular routes/destinations link grid (internal links to programmatic SEO pages).
Company, support, legal (Terms, Privacy, Cookie policy, Refund policy), social links, currency/locale, © Suskii Travels and Tour.

homepage_spec.mobile_app_home: Same content hierarchy adapted natively: search card with tab pills at top, bottom tab bar (Home, Trips, Deals, Prime, Account), pull-to-refresh deals, native date and passenger bottom sheets.

flights: Search (one-way, round-trip, multi-city), results list with filters (stops, airlines, times, price, duration, baggage, refundable) and sort (cheapest, fastest, best)
Fare details: baggage, fare rules, change/refund conditions, layover warnings (short connection, airport change, overnight, visa-required transit)
Passenger details with saved travellers, name validation against passport rules
Seat selection and extra baggage where supplier supports it
Book, hold (where supplier supports it), pay, ticket, e-ticket PDF + email + in-app
Manage booking: view, cancel, request change, request refund, add-ons
hotels: Search by city/hotel with rooms and child ages; map/list view; filters (price, stars, rating, free cancellation, amenities, area)
Hotel detail: gallery, rooms and rates, cancellation policy clearly shown, taxes and fees breakdown
packages: Admin-curated packages (flight + hotel + extras) with departures, inclusions/exclusions, itinerary, per-person pricing, deposit + installment options
tours: Tours and activities catalogue with dates, capacity, meeting point, cancellation rules, booking and QR voucher
visa: Eligibility checker (nationality x destination x purpose) from an admin-maintained rules table
Visa assistance products with required documents checklist, secure document upload (virus-scanned, encrypted, signed URLs), application status tracking, officer notes
Clear disclaimer: Suskii provides assistance; approval is by the issuing government
travel_addons: Travel insurance, airport transfers, eSIM, lounge access, extra baggage, seat selection; purchasable standalone or attached to a booking

modes: Book on hold: reserve where the supplier allows a hold, pay in full before the hold deadline
Installments: deposit + scheduled installments for packages, tours and visa services (inventory Suskii controls)
rules: Airline tickets are only issued after full payment; installment flights are only offered when a supplier hold or a Suskii-managed fare guarantee covers the gap. Record this in an ADR and surface it honestly in UI copy.

Show the full schedule, total cost and any fees before commitment; send reminders 3 days and 1 day before each due date; configurable grace period; automatic cancellation and refund policy applied on default.
Installment charges use saved payment authorisations only where the provider supports it; otherwise send payment links.

pricing_and_deals: MarkupRule engine (by vertical, route, airline, channel, user tier) managed in admin
Promo codes (percentage/fixed, caps, validity, usage limits per user and global, eligible verticals) with abuse protection
Deals worker: refresh cheapest fares for top routes every few hours, store snapshots with timestamps, drop stale deals automatically
Price alerts: user subscribes to a route; worker notifies on drop
suskii_prime: Plans (monthly/annual) sold via recurring billing on the payment provider
Benefits: member-only markups, service fee waivers, priority support queue, bonus wallet credit
Member badge in app; benefits applied in pricing module
accounts: Sign up/sign in with email + password, phone OTP, Google and Apple sign-in (Apple required on iOS if social login exists)
Guest checkout with booking lookup by reference + last name + email OTP
Profile, saved travellers, saved payment methods (provider tokens only), notification preferences, wallet, referrals, Prime status
Trips: upcoming, past, cancelled; downloadable documents; add to calendar
referrals_and_wallet: Referral codes, reward credit on referee's first completed trip, wallet ledger (double-entry), wallet usable at checkout, fraud checks on self-referrals
notifications: Transactional email, SMS/WhatsApp, push: booking confirmed, e-ticket ready, payment due, flight/schedule change, check-in reminder, refund status, price alert
support: Help center/FAQ from CMS, contact form, WhatsApp link, support tickets tied to bookings, SLA timers in admin
reviews: Verified-stay/trip reviews for hotels, tours and packages; moderation queue
admin_console: RBAC roles: super_admin, operations, finance, support, content_manager, visa_officer
Dashboards: bookings, revenue, conversion funnel, payment success rate, supplier error rate
Booking management: search, view timeline, resend documents, manual ticketing retry, cancel, refund (maker-checker approval for refunds above threshold)
Catalogue management: packages, tours, visa products and rules, add-ons, deals, promo codes, markups
CMS: banners, trust signals (with verified flag and evidence), destination content, FAQs
Users and Prime memberships, wallets, referrals
seo_and_growth: Programmatic SEO pages: /flights/{origin}-to-{destination}, /hotels/{city}, /visa/{country} with ISR and real cached data
Structured data (JSON-LD: Organization, WebSite SearchAction, FAQPage, Product/Offer where valid, BreadcrumbList)
Sitemaps, robots, canonical URLs, Open Graph images
Analytics: privacy-friendly product analytics (PostHog) with consent; server-side conversion events
ai_features_optional_phase: Natural-language search box ('cheap flight to Dubai in December for 2 adults') parsed by an LLM into the shared FlightSearch Zod schema via structured output/tool calling; always shown to the user as editable form fields before searching
Model choice: a fast, low-cost LLM behind an LlmProvider interface (cloud-agnostic); temperature 0; strict schema validation; fallback to the manual form on any parse failure
Guardrails: no PII sent to the LLM, prompt-injection-safe (LLM output is data, never executed), per-user rate limit and cost cap

security.standard: OWASP ASVS Level 2 as the baseline checklist; OWASP MASVS for the mobile app
authentication: Passwords hashed with argon2id; breached-password check (k-anonymity HIBP range API); minimum length 10
Short-lived access JWT (10-15 min, asymmetric signing, key rotation via JWKS) + rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection and family revocation
Web: tokens in httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookies + CSRF token for state-changing requests. Mobile: tokens in expo-secure-store only
Optional TOTP MFA for users; mandatory MFA for all admin accounts; admin console behind IP allowlist or SSO
Account lockout with exponential backoff; generic auth error messages; email and phone verification
Session/device management page with remote sign-out
authorization: RBAC + resource ownership checks on every booking/traveller/document endpoint (prevent IDOR); use non-sequential public IDs (UUIDv7 / ULID) and short booking references
Deny-by-default guards in NestJS; permissions tested in e2e suite
input_and_output: Zod validation on every request body, query and param; strip unknown fields
Prisma parameterised queries only; no raw SQL without tagged templates
Output encoding by React; sanitise any CMS rich text with DOMPurify server-side
File uploads: type sniffing, size limits, antivirus scan (ClamAV worker), stored private, served via short-lived signed URLs
transport_and_headers: Strict CSP with nonces (Next.js middleware), frame-ancestors none, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, Permissions-Policy
abuse_and_fraud: Rate limiting (Redis sliding window) per IP, user and route; stricter on auth, OTP, search and promo endpoints
Cloudflare Turnstile on sign-up, guest checkout, newsletter and booking lookup
Search scraping protection: per-IP search quotas, cache-first responses, bot scoring
Payment fraud signals: velocity, BIN country vs IP/geo mismatch, many cards per account, high-risk routes; flag for manual review in admin; 3-D Secure enforced by provider
Promo and referral abuse detection (device fingerprint hash, phone/email reuse)
payments: Hosted checkout / tokenised fields only (SAQ-A); never log payment payloads
Verify every webhook signature; store WebhookEvent by provider event id to deduplicate; process idempotently
Server-side amount verification: the amount paid must equal the server-computed amount for that booking and currency
Refunds require admin role + maker-checker above threshold; all money movements in a double-entry ledger
data_protection: Field-level encryption (envelope encryption with cloud KMS) for passport numbers, national IDs and visa documents
Encryption at rest for DB and storage; automated encrypted backups with tested restore runbook; PITR enabled
PII minimisation in logs (structured logger with redaction paths); SearchLog stores no personal data
Data retention jobs; DSAR export and deletion endpoints; cookie consent manager
secrets_and_supply_chain: Secrets in AWS Secrets Manager / GCP Secret Manager; injected at runtime; never in images or the mobile bundle
Dependabot/Renovate, pnpm audit, CodeQL or Semgrep SAST, Gitleaks secret scanning, Trivy container scanning, SBOM (CycloneDX) per release
Pinned base images by digest; non-root containers; read-only filesystem where possible
mobile_specific: No API secrets in the app; all supplier calls go through the backend
Play Integrity / App Attest verification on sensitive endpoints (login, payment init)
Disable screenshots on payment and document screens (Android FLAG_SECURE), clear sensitive state on background
Deep links validated (universal links / app links) with allowlisted paths; no tokens in URLs
security.audit: Immutable audit log for auth events, admin actions, booking state transitions, refunds and permission changes

tactics: RSC for static sections; client components only for interactive search module
ISR for deals and destination pages; Redis cache for search results (TTL 5-15 min per supplier guidance)
Streaming search results where suppliers return progressively
Image optimisation (AVIF/WebP, responsive sizes, priority only on LCP image)
Airport autocomplete served from an edge-cached static index for the top 500 airports, API fallback for the long tail
Mobile: Hermes, FlashList for results, lazy-load heavy screens, prefetch on intent

api_targets.note: Supplier searches run in parallel with per-supplier timeouts and circuit breakers; partial results are returned if one supplier fails.

accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA: keyboard navigable search module, visible focus rings, labelled inputs, ARIA for comboboxes and date pickers (use accessible patterns)
Touch targets >= 44x44; dynamic type support on mobile; screen reader labels on icon buttons
Automated axe checks in Playwright; manual VoiceOver/TalkBack pass before release
observability: Structured JSON logs (pino) with request IDs propagated web -> API -> workers
OpenTelemetry traces and metrics; export to Grafana Cloud / Datadog / cloud-native (configurable)
Sentry for web, mobile and API errors with PII scrubbing and source maps
Business metrics: search-to-book conversion, payment success rate, ticketing failure rate, supplier latency/error rate
Alerts: payment webhook failures, ticketing backlog, error-rate spikes, queue depth, DB connections

testing.unit: Vitest (packages, web) and Jest (API, mobile) with >= 80% coverage on pricing, money, booking state machine, installments, auth
testing.integration: API integration tests with Testcontainers (Postgres + Redis) and mocked supplier/payment adapters
testing.contract: OpenAPI schema diff check in CI; generated client must compile
testing.e2e_web: Playwright: search -> results -> passenger details -> mock payment -> confirmation; auth flows; accessibility scans
testing.e2e_mobile: Maestro flows for the same critical path
testing.security: OWASP ZAP baseline scan against staging; authz tests for IDOR on every resource
testing.load: k6 scenarios for search and checkout endpoints with thresholds
testing.visual: Storybook for ui-web with Chromatic or Playwright screenshot tests for key components

pipelines: PR: install (pnpm, cached) -> lint -> typecheck -> unit -> integration -> build affected (turbo --filter=...[origin/main]) -> SAST + secret scan -> preview deploy for web/admin
Main: all above + e2e against ephemeral environment -> build and sign Docker images -> Trivy scan -> push -> deploy to staging -> smoke tests

Release (tag): manual approval -> Prisma migrate deploy (backwards-compatible migrations only, expand/contract pattern) -> deploy to production with canary or rolling strategy -> automated rollback on failed health checks
Mobile: EAS Build on tag (preview profile for internal testers, production profile for stores), EAS Submit to TestFlight / Play internal track, EAS Update channels per environment
ci_cd.branch_protection: Required reviews, required checks, signed commits, no force-push to main

phases.name: Optional: AI trip search
tasks: Implement features.ai_features_optional_phase behind a feature flag with evals (a fixed set of 50 NL queries with expected parsed structs)
acceptance_criteria: >= 95% exact-match parse accuracy on the eval set
Graceful fallback on failure
Per-user cost cap enforced

edge_cases_to_handle: Offer expires between results and checkout -> re-search prompt with preserved inputs
Price increases or decreases at re-price -> explicit consent screen
Payment succeeds, redirect lost (user closes tab/app) -> webhook completes booking; user sees it in Trips and gets email
Duplicate payment attempts -> idempotency key + auto-refund of duplicates
Supplier timeout during ticketing -> reconciliation worker, never double-issue
Dates across timezones and date line; overnight arrivals shown as +1
Infant must be under 2 on the return date, not only on departure
Name length and character rules per airline; transliteration of non-ASCII names
Passport expiring within 6 months of travel -> warning
Currency switch mid-session -> re-price, charge only in the booking's settled currency
Installment default -> policy-driven cancellation with transparent refund calculation
Supplier schedule change after ticketing -> notify customer with accept/refund options
definition_of_done: Web, mobile and admin share one API and one set of schemas/types
Zero hardcoded secrets; all scans clean of high/critical issues
Docs complete: CLAUDE.md, README, ADRs, API docs, runbooks, threat model
A new developer can run the whole stack locally on Windows with docker compose and pnpm dev in under 15 minutes

Suskii Prime pricing and exact benefits
